stage1.impression: A calm, believable late-afternoon living room: the warm sun patches on the plaster, the window-bar shadows across the oak and the walnut credenza all hold together, and the pair reads at a glance at about half the frame's height. What gives it away as CG is the cabinets: they glow a neon, self-lit green that is brighter and more saturated than anything else the sun touches. The left speaker's cover is also cut in half by a hard shadow, so the two speakers no longer match, and the horn shadows on the wall make dull grey blobs that clutter the centre behind the turntable.

blocking_9: Cabinet acrylic reads as the real tint, not neon: side panels within delta E 2000 of 10 of #B2C9A2, with the inner batts no brighter than the sunlit plaster
The pair is lit as a pair: both woofer covers evenly lit, with no hard window-bar shadow splitting either one (left and right cover medians within 15 levels of each other)
Sun visibly passes through the cabinets: a green-tinted transmitted patch on the wall or floor beside each speaker that reads at a glance, not only a faint smear at the right
No grey shadow blobs on the wall behind the turntable and vase; the centre of the wall is clean for the heading
Shaded wall at right lifted so the right half of the frame does not sink to mid-grey (median 95 or more), and no crushed blacks at the window base

defects.what: Left cabinet's ribs and batts glow saturated neon green (RGB 115/165/88, delta E 15.3 against #B2C9A2); they look self-lit rather than lit by the sun
Right cabinet has the same neon green (116/178/90, delta E 14.3)
A hard vertical window-bar shadow splits the left woofer cover: right half lum 50 against left half 113, while the right speaker's cover is evenly lit at 125, so the pair does not match
The left horn's shadow lands as a dark grey blob on the wall behind the turntable and vase; it clutters the centre and is untinted
The right horn's shadow is an opaque grey blob (RGB 68/61/54) with only a faint green fringe; tinted resin should cast a tinted shadow
Shaded wall at the upper right sinks to lum 80, a muddy grey-brown that drags the right third down
Window frame base and sill crush to black (11.9% crushed)
A thin dark sliver of wall and window frame at the left edge reads as a cropping accident, not as framing
The only green light thrown into the room is a dim smear on the floor right of the right speaker (lum 44); the left speaker throws none
Cabinet edges render as heavy black outlines that frame each speaker like a drawn box (speaker material, see out_of_scope)

changes.problem: Both cabinets read as neon, self-lit green, which is the clearest sign that this is a render.

evidence.measured: RGB median 115/165/88, delta E 2000 15.27 against #B2C9A2; right side panel [1022,410,1035,600] delta E 14.32

change.to: 0.3 (and lower the bloom threshold's effect on greens: bloom 0.05 -> 0.03)

changes.expected: Side panels move toward a pale sage (about 140/175/120); the batts read as white fabric seen through tinted acrylic, not as a light source

changes.problem: A window-bar shadow splits the left woofer cover in half, so the pair is lit unequally.

evidence.measured: lum_median 49.6 (RGB 23/60/28) against 113 on the cover's left half and 124.5 on the right speaker's cover [1040,480,1170,580]

change.to: azimuth -70.0 deg, elevation 14.0 deg (re-check that no mullion shadow edge falls on either cover; if one does, move window 2 along the wall by 0.2 m)

changes.expected: Both covers evenly lit, medians within 15 levels; the sun rakes more across the room, so its beam passes through the cabinets and the horn shadows drop and move right, off the centre of the wall

changes.problem: The brief's idea, sun passing through both cabinets, barely shows: only a dim green smear at the right and nothing from the left speaker.

evidence.measured: lum_median 43.6, RGB 55/43/16 (barely green); the wall beside the right speaker [1210,400,1260,470] is a neutral 111/101/90

change.to: irradiance 48 W/m2, size 0.5 deg (with c2's angle), so that a crisp, saturated transmitted patch lands on the floor and wall beside each speaker

changes.expected: A readable green transmitted patch beside each speaker, on the floor or the lower wall, green-dominant (g above r by 15 or more)

changes.problem: The shaded right of the wall sinks to a muddy grey, so the frame is lopsided and the right speaker stands against dull mid-grey.

evidence.measured: lum_median 80.0 (RGB 86/79/70) against 224.9 in the sun patch [560,150,820,350]

changes.expected: Shade lifts by about 0.5 stop and keeps a slightly cool cast against the warm sun, so the light keeps its contrast without going muddy

changes.problem: The left horn's shadow lands as a grey blob behind the turntable and vase, cluttering the one place the eye rests between the speakers.

evidence.measured: lum_median 108.6 inside the blob against about 225 in the surrounding sun patch; the shape reads as an unexplained form

change.to: after c2, if the horn shadow still crosses the credenza top, move the speakers to x +/-1.3 and the vase to [0.55, 0.75, 0.56] so the shadow falls off the credenza run

changes.expected: The wall directly behind the turntable is lit and calm; the horn shadows fall to the right of each speaker

changes.problem: The base of the window frame and the sill crush to pure black at the lower left.

change.to: frame #5A5650 with a satin finish, so it picks up the sky and floor bounce

changes.expected: The frame reads as dark bronze-grey metal with visible edges, not as a hole

changes.problem: The corners are heavy enough at the lower left that the floor and window base go dead.

evidence.measured: foreground floor lum_p5 54.9 across [0,720,1440,810]; the lower-left corner is the darkest area outside the window

changes.expected: The floor's grain and the window-bar shadows stay legible to the corners

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn's tinted resin transmit light, so it casts a green-tinted shadow instead of an opaque grey one
out_of_scope.why: This is the horn's material (part of the speaker). It is fixed, but whoever owns the speaker's shading model should check its transmission

out_of_scope.request: Soften the near-black outline on the acrylic cabinet edges
out_of_scope.why: This is the cabinet's edge material and thickness, which belong to the speaker. In the image they draw a black box around each speaker and read as CG
